passages.title: A – Clean Parks Day
passages.text: On the first Saturday of every month, volunteers meet at the café in Hollins Park to pick up litter, clear paths and plant bulbs. It's a great way to get some fresh air and make new friends at the same time. Gloves and bags are provided, and there's tea and cake for everyone afterwards.

passages.title: B – Digital Buddies
passages.text: Many older people feel left out because they don't know how to use a smartphone or make video calls to their families. Could you help? We need patient volunteers who are good with technology to give one-to-one help at Elmwood Library every Wednesday afternoon. Sessions last two hours, and you can come every week or just occasionally.

passages.title: C – Willow Farm Animal Sanctuary
passages.text: Our sanctuary is home to more than 200 rescued animals, from horses and goats to rabbits and chickens. Volunteers help to feed the animals, clean their homes and sometimes assist our vet with health checks. We are open to volunteers aged 16 and over on Saturdays and Sundays, from 9 am to 3 pm.

passages.title: D – Brightstart Homework Club
passages.text: Our after-school club helps children aged 7 to 11 with their reading, maths and computer skills. Many of the children speak Arabic, Polish or Urdu at home, so volunteers who speak another language are especially welcome. The club runs every Wednesday afternoon from 3.30 to 5 pm at Ashby Primary School.

passages.title: E – Greenway Community Garden
passages.text: Turn an empty piece of land into a garden full of vegetables and flowers! Our volunteers – many of them retired – meet on Tuesday and Thursday mornings to dig, plant and harvest. No experience is needed. There's always a friendly chat over a cup of tea at break time, and you can take home some of the vegetables you've grown.

passages.title: F – Happy Paws Dog Rescue
passages.text: The dogs at our rescue centre love going for walks, but our staff don't always have time to take them out. Volunteer dog walkers must be at least 18 and able to come for two hours on a weekday, between 10 am and 4 pm. You'll get full training and a lot of grateful tails wagging!

passages.title: G – Riverside 10K Run
passages.text: We need 150 volunteers to help on the day of our annual charity race on Sunday 15 June. You could hand out water to runners, cheer them on at the side of the road or give out medals at the finish line. It's just one day, and you'll be part of an exciting sporting event. Everyone gets a free T-shirt!

passages.title: H – Northgate Welcome Centre
passages.text: We support families who have recently arrived in this country. Volunteers help them fill in forms, make phone calls and understand letters from schools and doctors. If you speak another language as well as English, especially Arabic, French or Farsi, we'd love to hear from you. We are open on Monday and Wednesday evenings from 6 to 9 pm.

questions.question: Zara is 17 and hopes to become a vet one day, so she wants to get some experience of working with animals. She is at school all week, so she can only help at weekends.
questions.explanation: At Willow Farm Animal Sanctuary volunteers 'feed the animals' and 'sometimes assist our vet', it accepts people 'aged 16 and over', and it is open 'on Saturdays and Sundays'. Happy Paws Dog Rescue also works with animals, but volunteers 'must be at least 18' and come 'on a weekday'.

questions.question: Brian has just retired and would like to spend time outdoors growing things. He's hoping to meet new people, and he'd prefer to help on weekday mornings.
questions.explanation: At Greenway Community Garden volunteers 'dig, plant and harvest', there's 'a friendly chat over a cup of tea', and they meet 'on Tuesday and Thursday mornings'. Clean Parks Day is also outdoors, includes planting bulbs and is a way to 'make new friends', but it takes place on Saturdays.

questions.question: Leila grew up speaking Arabic and French and would like to use her languages to help adults who are new to the country. She works during the day, so she is only free in the evenings.
questions.explanation: Northgate Welcome Centre supports 'families who have recently arrived in this country', wants volunteers who speak 'Arabic, French or Farsi', and is open 'on Monday and Wednesday evenings'. Brightstart Homework Club also welcomes volunteers who speak Arabic, but it helps children, not adults, and it runs on Wednesday afternoons.

questions.question: Sam is a university student who is very good with computers. He'd like to use his skills to help older people, and he has no lectures on Wednesday afternoons.
questions.explanation: Digital Buddies helps 'older people' who don't know how to use a smartphone, needs volunteers 'who are good with technology', and meets 'every Wednesday afternoon'. Brightstart Homework Club also teaches 'computer skills' on Wednesday afternoons, but it is for 'children aged 7 to 11', not older people.

questions.question: Nadia loves sport and would like to help at a big event. She can't promise to volunteer regularly, so she's looking for something that only takes one day.
questions.explanation: The Riverside 10K Run needs volunteers for 'an exciting sporting event', and 'It's just one day'. Clean Parks Day is also something she could do on a single day, but it means picking up litter and planting in a park, not helping at a sports event.
